reply.summary: Research artifact written to docs/designs/tasks/002-steam-windows-discovery/01-research.md. It covers the ADR-022 Windows backend contract, the existing SteamLinuxPlugin seams to share (keyvalues parser with \\-unescape, libraries_in_root, parse_manifest, canonical-path rule, degraded-scan/error semantics), the community-converged host-probing convention (HKCU\Software\Valve\Steam SteamPath stored forward-slash-delimited, HKLM SOFTWARE\Valve\Steam InstallPath in the 32-bit view, %ProgramFiles(x86)%/%ProgramFiles% defaults), WOW64 registry view flags (KEY_WOW64_32KEY/64KEY) and HKCU's shared nature, Windows path hazards (backslash separator justifying the mandated installdir refusal, reserved device names, \?\ canonicalize prefixes), the winreg-vs-windows-core dependency choice gateable via [target.'cfg(windows)'], and cross-compile compile-verification with cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. Every claim carries an inline source; key unknowns flagged for the designer: steamapps/ vs config/ libraryfolders.vdf location, registry value type/expansion, emitted-path \?\ handling, and the shared-core decomposition shape. Prior art: steam-game-path, Lutris config.py, Playmoir KB, Whisky docs, plus the repo's own Linux plugin. Sources read within budget: 8 repo files plus the ADR/task pair; external citations verified via targeted web lookups.
reply.commitMessage: docs: add research for T-002 Windows Steam discovery
docs: design the Windows Steam discovery plugin (T-002)

findings.location: Assumption register, row A1 ("Everything after root selection is the same on Windows as on Linux: … and library `path` values written with doubled backslashes. | verified | …github.com/Playmoir/knowledge-base/blob/main/steam-library-integration.md")
findings.problem: The citation is dead: github.com/Playmoir/knowledge-base and the GitHub API both return 404 (no such repository), as does the raw.githubusercontent.com form. It is the only live-checkable support for the doubled-backslash `path` spelling and the second of A1's two bases (the other is a StackOverflow question that returns 403 to a non-browser client, so it is inconclusive rather than confirming). A1 is the row that licenses the document's central move — putting everything after root selection into one shared module — so a `verified` row resting on a nonexistent source fails the register's own standard. A19 and §2's second-location paragraph cite it too, but A19 stands on its other basis, which I verified live (lutris util/steam/config.py reads config/libraryfolders.vdf).
findings.fix: In A1, swap the Playmoir URL for a live source that shows a Windows libraryfolders.vdf `path` value with escaped backslashes, or split the `path`-spelling clause out of A1 and mark it `unverified`, noting that A2's verified `\`/`"` unescape (keyvalues.rs:186-207) is what makes either spelling arrive usable.

findings.location: §5 Root candidates ("2. `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Valve\Steam` → `InstallPath`: the 32-bit-view result, then the 64-bit-view result if the first was `None`") against §1's `pub enum RegistryKey { CurrentUserValveSteam, LocalMachineValveSteam }` and Test strategy #3 ("HKLM-32-bit-view only; HKLM-64-bit-view only")
findings.problem: The three sections disagree about who owns the WOW64 view choice. §3 puts the 32-then-64 fallback inside `registry_string_value`, which is `#[cfg(windows)]`-only, so `host_candidates` gets exactly one value per key and cannot order "the 32-bit-view result, then the 64-bit-view result" as §5 states. And a fake keyed by `(RegistryKey, &str)` (§4's HashMap over that key) cannot express 32-view-only versus 6-view-only, so the two named Test strategy #3 cases are unwritable as specified. Consequence: the view-ordering policy — the answer to A4 and the stated reason for rejecting the hardcoded `Wow6432Node` spelling — is covered only by #12's type-check and #13's manual run.
findings.fix: Put the view in the seam so `host_candidates` orders it: add `LocalMachineValveSteam32` and `LocalMachineValveSteam64` variants (candidate order HKCU, HKLM-32, HKLM-64, envs) and reduce `registry_string_value` to "open this key with these flags, read one REG_SZ", keeping #3's two cases as written; or delete those two cases from #3 and state in §5 and Risks that view ordering is compile- and manually-verified only.

findings.location: §8 CLI wiring, else-branch comment "// `--steam-root` is the Linux seam from T-001: the row's platform tag is the plugin's, so the plugin is the one that follows the flag."
findings.problem: With `--steam-root` the Windows plugin is not registered at all, so no `steam-windows` row can ever come from an explicit root. That contradicts the task's Done-when clause docs/tasks/T-002-steam-windows-discovery.md:65-67 — "…and `--steam-root` keeps working for it" — where "it" is the steam-windows plugin. §8 concedes the gap ("A user who wants `steam-windows`-tagged rows from an explicit root is a one-line CLI change with its own argument") and the Deferred item "An explicit 'these roots are Windows Steam roots' CLI seam" hands it to no document, so this is a deferral against a stated requirement, not an out-of-scope refinement.
findings.fix: Smallest fix that keeps the three CLI tests undoubled: in the `--steam-root` branch register `SteamWindowsPlugin::from_roots(steam_root.iter().cloned())` instead of the Linux plugin when compiled for Windows (`#[cfg(windows)]`), so the flag feeds the plugin whose rows that host can produce, and drop §8's self-imposed "no `#[cfg]` in `main.rs`". Otherwise register it alongside the Linux plugin and say in §8 and Test strategy #9 that the fixture rows double to eight and cli_tests.rs:68-72/:124 are re-pinned across both tags. Either way, record the reading of :66-67 in the Revision log instead of in Deferred.

findings.location: §5 Root candidates — "A relative value is ignored by the same `absolute_env` helper Linux uses (crates/discovery/src/steam_linux.rs:338-342)"
findings.problem: `absolute_env` is a private `fn` in `steam_linux.rs`, and §1's inventory of what moves into `steam_common` (library_paths, libraries_in_root_with_skips, scan_library, read_text_file, canonical_paths, discovered_game, parse_manifest/usable_install_dir) omits it, while §1 keeps `host_candidates` in `steam_linux`. As specified, steam_windows's `host_candidates` can neither call nor share that helper, and copying it is the duplication the Done-when clause forbids.
findings.fix: Add `absolute_env` to §1's moved-items list (`steam_common`, `pub(crate)`), with steam_linux's call sites rewired to it.

findings.location: §5 Root candidates — "each only when the variable is set and absolute", read together with §6's "`Path::is_absolute` (which reads a Windows path as relative on a Linux host)" and Test strategy #3
findings.problem: The env-candidate gate is `absolute_env`, whose predicate is `PathBuf::is_absolute` — host-dependent, as §6 itself states. `host_candidates` is compiled and tested on Linux (§3, Test strategy #3), so on the test host the gate can only pass with POSIX-absolute fake values, leaving the Windows-shaped value the design is about (`C:\Program Files (x86)`) either untested or silently dropped by the very rule under test.
findings.fix: State in §5 which values the fake supplies and add one #3 case pinning what a Windows-absolute value does on each host — best done by generalizing the absoluteness check over `SteamTarget` next to `install_dir_rejects_backslash`, so the rule exercised on Linux is the rule that runs on Windows.

findings.location: §1 sketch — "impl DiscoveryPlugin for SteamWindowsPlugin { /* delegates to `core`, name() = \"steam-windows\" */ }" versus §2's "prefix is `T::NAME`, which is the same string the plugin's `name()` returns, so the prefix can no longer drift"
findings.problem: The §2 no-drift claim only holds if the plugin's `name()` returns `T::NAME`; the §1 sketch shows a second literal spelling of the tag beside `WindowsTarget::NAME`, which is exactly the duplicate §2 says is gone.
findings.fix: Write `name()` as `self.core.name()` in the §1 sketch for both plugins, so the single-source claim is the shape on the page.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "Windows, 32-bit (x86) host | unknown" and "Windows, ARM64 host | unknown"
findings.problem: Two matrix rows carry `unknown` status. Checklist rule 1 treats `unknown` as a major finding: every row must carry a decision. The uncertainties behind these cells (A20's 32-bit view-flag behavior, no ARM64 exercise) are already carried in Risks, and both hosts plausibly work via the non-redirected HKCU read (A5) and degrade safely otherwise, so a status with a caveat is available.
findings.fix: Replace both `unknown` cells with `Partial`: 32-bit — "HKCU candidate and scan work (A5); the HKLM 64-bit-view query (A20) and the absent `%ProgramFiles(x86)%` fallback are unexercised"; ARM64 — "same code path as x64 (A4's model); not exercised in this run" — keeping the verification caveat in Risks rather than in the status.

findings.location: §8 CLI wiring — "engine.register_plugin(Box::new(SteamLinuxPlugin::from_roots(steam_root.iter().cloned())));"
findings.problem: On a Windows host, `discovery list --steam-root <root>` registers only SteamLinuxPlugin; the Windows plugin never runs on that branch, so no CLI path emits `steam-windows` rows from explicit roots and Windows Steam roots get rows tagged `SteamLinux`. This contradicts the task's Done-when clause "`--steam-root` keeps working for it" (docs/tasks/T-002-steam-windows-discovery.md:65-67), and the Deferred entry ("An explicit 'these roots are Windows Steam roots' CLI seam") hands off a requirement the source states outright. The Options-considered rejection only rules out sharing the flag across both plugins on every host (which would double cli_tests.rs:68-72's four-row assertion); it does not cover the Windows-host case.
findings.fix: Make the `--steam-root` branch target-aware: one `#[cfg(windows)]` passes `steam_root` to `SteamWindowsPlugin::from_roots` on Windows and keeps `SteamLinuxPlugin::from_roots` on Linux, leaving Linux behavior and all three CLI tests byte-identical; delete §8's "host-agnostic — no `#[cfg]` in `main.rs`" sentence accordingly.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix / Test strategy #12 — "Cross-compile to `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` | Yes"
findings.problem: The row claims support while #12 makes the gnu check a "local alternative" that CI never runs, so no named gate answers the row.
findings.fix: Mark the row `Partial (local only)` or fold a one-time gnu `cargo check` into Rollout #4's local gate list.

findings.location: §5 Root candidates — "no normalization happens here — the canonical-path rule is what turns both into one comparable spelling" (with the Risks row "A candidate must canonicalize and contain a `steamapps/` directory before anything under it is read")
findings.problem: On Windows the first contact with a candidate root is std::fs::canonicalize, which opens the path; a registry-sourced candidate in server-service form (\\server\share — any same-user process can write HKCU\Software\Valve\Steam\SteamPath as a plain REG_SZ, which §4's REG_SZ-only rule returns) triggers an outbound SMB session with the user's NTLM credentials to the named server, and can stall the CLI on an unreachable host, before the gate rejects the candidate. The stated mitigation covers what is read behind the gate, not the gate's own side effect, so §3's "Reading is the only thing that can fail, and a failure is 'no candidate', never an error" is untrue in the sense of 'without effect'. Exploitability is bounded (a same-user registry writer can coerce SMB auth itself), hence minor.
findings.fix: In host_candidates' Windows arm, syntactically refuse candidate roots that are not drive-absolute local paths (equivalently, drop UNC-form \\… candidates) before the list reaches the canonical-path rule — replacing canonicalize-as-first-contact with a one-line syntax check that every legitimate registry/env candidate (A3, A6) passes.

findings.location: §5 Root candidates — "no candidate needs a separate existence gate (§2's canonical-path rule drops what is not there), and `canonical_paths` collapses the common case where the registry points at the default folder, so a double-listed root costs nothing."
findings.problem: "costs nothing" is established only for the identical-path case. Verified for that case: canonical_paths (crates/discovery/src/steam_linux.rs:322-334) canonicalizes into a BTreeSet, so a registry SteamPath and the %ProgramFiles(x86)% default that resolve to the same folder collapse before any scanning. When they resolve to different folders — Steam on another drive with a leftover %ProgramFiles(x86)%\Steam that still has a steamapps/ directory — both roots survive and each is scanned in full: one libraryfolders.vdf read capped at keyvalues::MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES = 1 MiB (keyvalues.rs:21, applied pre-allocation at steam_linux.rs:290-298), then per library only that root declares a read_dir plus one metadata+read per appmanifest_*.acf (steam_linux.rs:200-231). Library-level de-dup over the union of roots' libraries (steam_linux.rs:64-70) bounds the overlap, so the real cost is small — but the design asserts it away instead of stating the bound, in the very section the Deferred registry-key and BaseInstallFolder_N items will later be edited against.
findings.fix: Replace "so a double-listed root costs nothing" in the same sentence with the bound: "…so a double-listed root collapses to one scan; when the registry and the env default are different roots, each extra root costs at most one 1 MiB-capped libraryfolders.vdf read plus, for the libraries only it declares, one read_dir and one capped read per manifest — and discover() de-dups the libraries roots share (crates/discovery/src/steam_linux.rs:64-70), so no library is scanned twice." No mechanism added, no candidate ordering changed.

findings.location: Chosen design §8 (else-branch: "engine.register_plugin(Box::new(SteamLinuxPlugin::from_roots(steam_root.iter().cloned())));") and the Deferred bullet "An explicit 'these roots are Windows Steam roots' CLI seam that would emit `steam-windows` rows from any host (§8): no follow-up yet."
findings.problem: [new] The deferral contradicts the task's Done-when: "The `steam-windows` plugin is wired into `apps/discovery-cli` (`discovery list`) alongside `steam-linux`, and `--steam-root` keeps working for it" (docs/tasks/T-002-steam-windows-discovery.md:65-67), whose subject is the steam-windows plugin. Under §8 the `--steam-root` branch never registers `SteamWindowsPlugin`, so no `steam-windows`-tagged row can ever result from the flag, and the design defers exactly that behavior. The proposal's rebuttal (doubling CLI assertions, "a platform tag that is a fiction on a Linux runner") is unsound: the protected assertions live in `apps/discovery-cli/tests`, while the task freezes only the Linux plugin's tests (T-002:34-35), and the design's own rule "the row's platform tag is the plugin's" gives the doubled rows a defined meaning.
findings.fix: Register both plugins on the roots branch: add `engine.register_plugin(Box::new(SteamWindowsPlugin::from_roots(steam_root.iter().cloned())));` beside the Linux one in §8, update the row-count assertions in `apps/discovery-cli/tests/cli_tests.rs` to the doubled expectation, and delete the Deferred bullet. If the author instead reads the clause as merely "the flag keeps working on Linux", surface that as an explicit task-deviation question for the runner rather than keeping it inside the document's Deferred list.

findings.location: Test strategy #2 — "`steam_windows::usable_install_dir` and `steam_linux::usable_install_dir` differ on no other case."
findings.problem: [new] The test requires `steam_linux::usable_install_dir` to be public; it is private today (crates/discovery/src/steam_linux.rs:275), is absent from A15's preserved-surface list, and Non-goals freeze "Any change to `SteamLinuxPlugin`'s ... `pub` items" — so either §1's public-surface-preservation claim breaks or the test cannot be written. The new public item would also have no consumer besides this differential test, growing public surface without need.
findings.fix: Test the one-rule difference solely through the already-public `parse_manifest` on both sides (the first half of #2, backslash `installdir` yielding `None` vs `Some`, already establishes it) and delete the `usable_install_dir` comparison clause from #2; keep `usable_install_dir` `pub(crate)` in `steam_common`.

reply.summary: Major findings consumed: (correctness r1c0 #1) A1's dead Playmoir citation removed — A1 narrowed to the VDF-shape/field-set claim on the surviving citation and the doubled-backslash spelling split out as A1b `unverified` with A2's unescape as basis; the dead URL also deleted from A19. (#2) View ordering moved into the seam: `RegistryKey` now carries `LocalMachineValveSteam32/64` variants ordered by pure `host_candidates` (§5), `registry_string_value` opens one (key, view) per call (§3), §4 and Test strategy #8 re-pinned to three variants, making #3's 'HKLM-32-bit-view only / 64-bit-view only' cases writable. (#3, and compatibility #1 / complexity #1, same finding) §8's roots branch is host-aware via one `#[cfg]` pair so `--steam-root` registers `SteamWindowsPlugin` on Windows (task Done-when :65-67); the contradictory Deferred bullet, the 'no #[cfg] in main.rs' sentence, and the Options rebuttal's fiction argument are deleted; the clause reading is recorded in the Revision log, superseding r0: q8. (compatibility #1) Both `unknown` matrix cells became `Partial` with the caveats left to Risks. Cheap minors folded in: absolute_env added to §1's moved list, #2's public `usable_install_dir` differential-test clause deleted (resolving the Non-goals/A15 conflict), `name()` in the sketch written as `self.core.name()`, and the gnu matrix row marked `Partial (local only)` with a one-time local check owned by Rollout #4. The diff is net-positive (~+9 lines) because three majors required new structure — a third enum variant in sketches and prose, two cfg'd registration lines, and the A1b register row — which the deletions (Deferred bullet, test clause, dead citations, hedged claims) only partly offset.
reply.commitMessage: docs: revise T-002 proposal for round-1 design review findings

findings.location: §5 Root candidates — "A relative value is ignored by the same `absolute_env` helper Linux uses, shared per §1" read with Test strategy #3 (re-raised from r0; the sentence was changed but the gap remains)
findings.problem: The env-candidate gate's predicate is `PathBuf::is_absolute` (crates/discovery/src/steam_linux.rs:341), host-dependent as §6 itself states. `host_candidates` is compiled and unit-tested on Linux, so the fake can only pass POSIX-absolute values, and the Windows branch of the rule — a `C:\Program Files (x86)`-shaped value kept, a Windows-relative one dropped — is exercised on no host. §5 still does not state what values the fake supplies. Runtime behavior is correct on each host; this is a verification gap for a rule the design depends on, unchanged by the revision.
findings.fix: In §5, add one sentence stating that the #3 fake supplies POSIX-absolute values and that the Windows-absolute case is covered only by gates #12/#13; or generalize the absoluteness predicate over `SteamTarget` next to `install_dir_rejects_backslash` (§1's existing mechanism) and add one Test strategy #3 case pinning what a Windows-shaped value does on each host.

findings.location: Test strategy #2 — "`foo\bar`, the doubled form `foo\\bar` as a real Windows ACF writes it (A2)"
findings.problem: The r1 revision split the doubled-backslash spelling out as A1b, marked `unverified` with "the design assumes no spelling" — yet this body sentence still asserts the doubled spelling as what real Windows ACFs write, and cites A2, which is the reader's verified `\`/`"` unescape behavior (keyvalues.rs:186-207), not a source on what ACFs write. The changed register makes this sentence unsupported; the test case itself stays valid either way, so it is a factual/language defect, not behavioral.
findings.fix: Reword to "the doubled form a Windows writer may emit (A1b, spelling unverified)", leaving the enumerated test cases unchanged.

findings.location: Chosen design §8 — "#[cfg(windows)] engine.register_plugin(Box::new(SteamWindowsPlugin::from_roots(steam_root.iter().cloned())));" and Options — "§8 instead feeds the flag to the plugin of the compiled-for host, where the task's ':65-67' clause is met"
findings.problem: [new] The branch the revision now cites as satisfying the task's Done-when "`--steam-root` keeps working for it" (docs/tasks/T-002-steam-windows-discovery.md:65-67) is executed by no gate the design names. It is compiled out on Linux, so *Test strategy* #9/#10 cannot reach it; #12 only type-checks it (cargo check --all-targets compiles the bin but runs nothing); and #13's manual Windows check enumerates only "the default install, any secondary library, the `\\?\` prefix in `install_path`, and a non-default install path from the registry" — no `--steam-root` — with *Rollout* #5 pointing at the same list. The revision therefore replaced the Deferred bullet with a Done-when clause resting on one statement of unexercised code, unlike the document's own convention of naming the lone gate per Windows-only row (Compatibility matrix gnu row: "*Rollout* #4 runs the `cargo check` for it once"). My r1 major is not re-raised as such: the deferral is gone and the doubling rebuttal checks out against apps/discovery-cli/tests/cli_tests.rs:68-72, :91, :124, which all pass --steam-root at the fixture and assert exactly four rows.
findings.fix: Add "`discovery list --steam-root <that install>`" to *Test strategy* #13's enumerated checks and name #13 in *Rollout* #5 as the lone gate for §8's Windows roots branch; point §8's "keeps working for it" sentence at that gate instead of at #12.

findings.location: Chosen design §5 — "`HKLM\SOFTWARE\Valve\Steam` → `InstallPath` as two ordered candidates: `LocalMachineValveSteam32` then `LocalMachineValveSteam64` (A4); values are appended in that order" vs Test strategy #3 — "both keys present (HKCU `SteamPath` first, HKLM `InstallPath` second, then the two env candidates)"
findings.problem: [new] The r1 seam change made both HKLM views unconditional candidates, but #3's ordered-list enumeration was not updated: it still expects four entries where the revised rule yields five once both views answer. The two new consequences of always appending both views are also unpinned — the same path reported by both views (§5's "collapses both views reporting one path" is prose only; #3's dedupe clause covers registry-vs-env equality only, though the BTreeSet in canonical_paths, crates/discovery/src/steam_linux.rs:322-333, does back it), and distinct paths from the two views, which now scans two roots where the superseded short-circuit scanned one.
findings.fix: Restate #3's "both keys present" expectation as the five-entry ordered list and add one enumerated case — both HKLM views reporting, same path vs distinct paths — with the expected candidate list for each.

findings.location: Chosen design §3 — "Which HKLM view to ask first is `host_candidates`' policy, not the reader's (§5)"
findings.problem: [new] "ask first" carries over the superseded fallback wording (r0 asked the 64-bit view "if the first was `None`"); under §5's always-append rule there is an order, not a first/second branch, and Test strategy #8 asserts "exactly the three `RegistryKey` variants" are queried, which a short-circuiting implementation would violate whenever the 32-bit view answers.
findings.fix: Say "which HKLM views to ask, and in what order" so the sentence cannot be read as license for a short-circuit that contradicts #8.

reply.summary: Major (§8 unexercised roots branch): the fix is gate-naming, not new machinery — Test strategy #13 now enumerates `discovery list --steam-root <non-default install>` and is declared the only gate that runs §8's `#[cfg(windows)]` roots branch; Rollout #5's parenthetical widened to cover the task's :65-67 clause beside :72-74; §8's closing sentence now points at #13/Rollout #5 instead of resting on #12, and its loose "byte-for-byte T-001's" claim was narrowed to "keeps T-001's one-plugin shape". Minor (#3 vs §5's five-entry list): #3's "both keys present" expectation restated as HKCU `SteamPath`, then both HKLM views' `InstallPath` in §5's order, then the two env candidates, plus an explicit "both views answering" case pinning same-path collapse and distinct-paths → two roots; the old registry-vs-env dedupe clause was consolidated into it rather than duplicated. Nit (§3 "view to ask first"): reworded to "which HKLM views to ask, and in what order", so it cannot license a short-circuit that contradicts #8. Offsets keep the diff at 592 lines net-zero: the §8 code comment duplicating the Compatibility matrix's Linux-host row, §5's duplicated `\\?\` claim (canonical in §7), and §5 item 3's wording were compressed. Revision log updated by superseding the two existing r1 entries in place (seam ordering now cites Test strategy #3; the `--steam-root` entry now names #13 via Rollout #5), no stacked entries, no new line budget.
reply.commitMessage: docs: name the manual --steam-root gate and pin both HKLM view candidates

findings.location: Test strategy #3 — "both views answering (one path from both → one root after the canonical-path rule, distinct paths → two roots and rows from two installs)"
findings.problem: [new] The enumeration's other cases state expectations at the level of the named gate (a candidate list from a pure `host_candidates` — §5: "no filesystem access"; #3: "pure, fake registry + fake env"), but this case, added to answer my r1 minor, states downstream results — "one root after the canonical-path rule" and "rows from two installs" are outputs of `canonical_paths`/`discover()`, which a pure `host_candidates` call cannot produce. No fixture backs "two installs" (only `crates/discovery/tests/fixtures/steam/minimal` is scannable, and #5 says "no new fixture tree is introduced"), and no existing Linux test pins the two-equal-roots root-level collapse (the dedup test at steam_linux_tests.rs:162 is library-level; no test passes `from_roots` two roots), so as written the collapse consequence my r1 minor asked to pin could end up asserted by nobody. The revision shows the right level elsewhere in the same edit, trimming the registry==env case to the pure form "not deduped by `host_candidates` (§5)".
findings.fix: State the case's expectation at #3's level — equal values from both views → both appended in §5's order; distinct values → both entries appended in §5's order — and pin the downstream consequence in #4, where the fake registry points both HKLM variants at the same `minimal` fixture root and the four games (not eight) come back; drop "rows from two installs" or replace it with the distinct-values candidate list rather than sanctioning a second install fixture #5 refuses.

findings.location: §5 Root candidates — "a relative value is ignored by `absolute_env` (§1)" read with Test strategy #3 (re-raised; unchanged by this revision)
findings.problem: The env-candidate gate's predicate is `PathBuf::is_absolute` (crates/discovery/src/steam_linux.rs:338-341), host-dependent as §6 states, and `host_candidates` is unit-tested only on Linux, so the fake can supply only POSIX-absolute values; the Windows half of the rule (a `C:\…`-shaped value kept, a Windows-relative one dropped) is exercised on no host. The revision rewrote the sentence without closing the gap, and the Revision log records no decision on it. This is a persistent verification gap, not a break introduced by the revisions; runtime behavior is correct on each host.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to §5 (or #3) stating the #3 fake supplies POSIX-absolute values and Windows-absolute coverage sits with gates #12/#13; or generalize the absoluteness predicate over `SteamTarget` beside `install_dir_rejects_backslash` and add one #3 case pinning a Windows-shaped value's outcome per host.

findings.location: Test strategy #2 — "the doubled form `foo\\bar` as a real Windows ACF writes it (A2)" (re-raised; text untouched by this diff)
findings.problem: The sentence still asserts as fact the doubled-backslash spelling that A1b marks `unverified` with "the design assumes no spelling", and cites A2, which is the `\`/`"` unescape behavior (keyvalues.rs:186-207), not a source on what ACFs write. The register-side closure in the revision log did not propagate to this body sentence, leaving register and body in contradiction. The test case itself remains valid under any spelling.
findings.fix: Reword to "the doubled form a Windows writer may emit (A1b, spelling unverified)", leaving the enumerated test cases unchanged.

findings.location: Test strategy #3 (changed text) — "both views answering (one path from both → one root after the canonical-path rule, distinct paths → two roots and rows from two installs)"
findings.problem: The named sub-outcomes are produced by `from_registry_and_roots`' filesystem pass (§3), not by the pure `host_candidates` candidate list this item's header ("pure, fake registry + fake env") scopes; "rows from two installs" additionally needs two fixture trees that no test item owns.
findings.fix: Scope #3 to the candidate list ("two distinct candidates, ordered") and attach the rows-from-two-installs outcome to #4's `from_registry_and_roots` harness, or drop it.

findings.location: Test strategy #3 (`steam_windows::host_candidates` unit list) — "both views answering (one path from both → one root after the canonical-path rule, distinct paths → two roots and rows from two installs)"
findings.problem: The newly added dual-view case asserts outcomes at a layer that cannot produce them: §5 defines host_candidates as "pure — registry and environment are lookups, no filesystem access", so it never canonicalizes; the collapse-to-one-root and "rows from two installs" results belong to from_registry_and_roots/SteamCore::with_roots. The second half also needs two valid Steam roots, but the fixture trees are crates/discovery/tests/fixtures/steam/minimal and .../steam/all-broken (the latter exists to produce the error case, #6), and #5 states "no new fixture tree is introduced". Since #3 is the named evidence for the Compatibility matrix row "Windows x64 whose Valve key exists only under `WOW6432Node` | Yes", that row currently rests on an assertion that cannot be run as written.
findings.fix: In #3 keep only "both views answering → both values appended, LocalMachineValveSteam32 before LocalMachineValveSteam64, not deduped"; move the "one path from both → one root" collapse into #4 (from_registry_and_roots with the fake registry pointing both views at the same fixture root) and delete "distinct paths → two roots and rows from two installs" rather than adding a fixture tree.

findings.location: Chosen design §5 (Root candidates) — "Registry values arrive in mixed case and either slash form (A3, A4)"
findings.problem: The cited assumptions no longer support the sentence: A3 records the opposite for the HKCU value ("stored lowercase with forward slashes") and A4 states nothing about case or slash form. The r1 A1b revision dropped the analogous spelling assumption for ACF paths; here one asserted spelling was replaced by a broader one instead of dropping the assertion. Behaviour is unaffected (no normalization happens in §5; §7's canonical-path rule absorbs either form).
findings.fix: Reword to "Registry values arrive in whatever case and slash form the installer wrote (A3 records one observed spelling; no spelling is assumed) — the canonical-path rule is what turns both into one comparable spelling (§7)."

findings.location: Test strategy #13 (manual Windows gate) — "the only gate for §8's roots branch"
findings.problem: Overstates against §8's own "the Windows branch is type-checked by #12 and run only by #13": #12's cargo check --workspace --all-targets --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc compiles that #[cfg(windows)] branch, so #13 is not the only gate on any reading.
findings.fix: Say "the only run gate for §8's roots branch (#12 only type-checks it)".

findings.location: §5 Root candidates — "`canonical_paths` collapses the common case where the registry points at the default folder, so a double-listed root costs nothing."
findings.problem: re-raised (unchanged in substance; the r1 revision rewrote the line it sits on). The sentence still establishes the cost only for the identical-path collapse, and this round the paragraph's scope widened: candidate item 2 now appends two HKLM-view values ('as two ordered candidates'), and Test strategy #3 now pins 'distinct paths → two roots and rows from two installs'. So the paragraph governs three doubling sources (registry vs env default, HKLM 32-bit view vs 64-bit view, the two env defaults against each other) while the cost claim still covers one. When two candidates resolve to different existing folders — Steam on another drive with a leftover %ProgramFiles(x86)%\Steam\steamapps, or a stale 64-bit-view InstallPath at a previous install — both roots survive and each is scanned: one libraryfolders.vdf read capped at 1 MiB (crates/discovery/src/keyvalues.rs:21, applied pre-allocation at crates/discovery/src/steam_linux.rs:287-298), then per library only that root declares a read_dir plus one metadata+read per appmanifest_*.acf (steam_linux.rs:200-231). Library-level de-dup over the union of roots' libraries (steam_linux.rs:61-71) bounds the overlap, so the real cost is small; the finding is that the design asserts it away in the very section that decides to append candidates with no existence gate.
findings.fix: Replace 'so a double-listed root costs nothing' with the bound, once, covering all three sources: '…so candidates that resolve to one folder collapse to one scan; when two resolve to different folders that both exist, each extra root costs at most one 1 MiB-capped libraryfolders.vdf read plus, for the libraries only it declares, one read_dir and one capped read per manifest — and discover() de-dups the libraries roots share (crates/discovery/src/steam_linux.rs:61-71), so no library is scanned twice.' No mechanism added, no candidate set or ordering changed.

findings.location: crates/discovery/src/steam_windows.rs:153-158
findings.problem: Registry-sourced root candidates (HKCU SteamPath, HKLM InstallPath values) are appended verbatim with no absolute-path gate, while the env candidates pass through absolute_env. A corrupt or hostile registry value with a relative path resolves against the process working directory in canonical_paths, steering the read-only scan there — the residual loose end of the design's 'corrupt or hostile registry value' Risks row, and an asymmetry with the env handling. Impact is bounded (candidate must canonicalize and carry a steamapps/ directory; scan is read-only and size-capped; HKCU write access implies user-level code execution), so this is hardening, not a violated requirement.
findings.fix: Gate registry values with the same absolute check used for env values (push only when PathBuf::from(value).is_absolute(), ideally via a shared helper), and pin 'a relative registry value contributes no candidate' as a unit test beside host_candidates_ignores_a_relative_env_value.
